title: Deconstruction and Its Critics
text:
Deconstruction, associated with Jacques Derrida, questions the assumption that a text has a single stable meaning. Critics who use this method look for tensions and contradictions within a work, showing how its language undermines its own claims.

Critics of deconstruction argue that it can lead to relativism, since every reading seems equally valid. Its defenders reply that it does not deny meaning; instead, it reveals how meaning depends on context, language, and the reader's position.

options: the assumption that a text has a single stable meaning

questions.text: What do critics of deconstruction argue it can lead to?
options: relativism, because every reading seems equally valid

questions.text: Why do defenders say deconstruction does not deny meaning?
options: because they claim meaning depends on context, language and the reader's position
because they believe nobody reads texts
because the author alone fixes meaning

questions.text: What can a deconstructive critic reveal by looking at tensions in a text?
options: that the language may undermine the text's own claims
that the book is too long
that the reader must agree with the critic

vocabulary.translation: analysis that exposes contradictions in a text
vocabulary.definition: a method that questions stable meaning in texts

vocabulary.translation: the view that all interpretations are equally valid
vocabulary.definition: the idea that truth depends on the viewpoint
